description: Six-panel composite of bright-field transmission electron micrographs (TEM) documenting the evolution of dislocation substructures with tensile strain; the group is mixed in content (4 austenite panels, 2 ferrite panels, plus one TEM inset) but all panels are the same modality. Every panel carries a white label box with the strain level and a black scale bar. (a) "5 %" austenite, 0.5 µm bar: one straight set of parallel slip lines marked by a dashed line labelled (1-11), with a bottom-right inset (0.2 µm bar) resolving finer parallel slip lines. (b) "10 %" and (c) "20 %" austenite, 0.5 µm bars: two intersecting dashed traces labelled (1-11) and (11-1), i.e. multidirectional slip within one grain. (d) "40 %" austenite, 0.5 µm bar: a single dominant slip direction labelled (11-1) with visibly narrower slip-line spacing than (a). (e) "5 %" ferrite, 1 µm bar: diffuse tangled dislocations and loose dislocation arrangements; (f) "40 %" ferrite, 1 µm bar: dense, dark, cell-like dislocation tangles. The figure demonstrates that austenite deforms by planar slip on {111} while ferrite deforms by wavy slip forming dislocation cells. No numeric strain values beyond the panel labels and no magnification numbers are printed.

observations.observation: The group consists of six TEM micrographs labelled (a) through (f), each stamped with a tensile-strain percentage (5 %, 10 %, 20 %, 40 %) and a black scale bar.
Panel (a) (5 %) bears a 0.5 µm scale bar and a dashed line annotated (1-11), and contains a bottom-right inset with a separate 0.2 µm scale bar showing finer parallel slip lines.
Panels (b) (10 %) and (c) (20 %) each show two dashed traces intersecting at an angle, annotated (1-11) and (11-1), while panel (d) (40 %) shows only one labelled slip direction, (11-1).
The slip-line spacing visible in panel (d) (40 %) is noticeably smaller than that in panel (a) (5 %).
Panels (e) (5 %) and (f) (40 %) carry 1 µm scale bars, larger than the 0.5 µm bars of the austenite panels (a–d).
The ferrite substructure in (f) (40 %) appears as dense dark tangled walls enclosing lighter cell interiors, whereas (e) (5 %) shows dispersed, loosely tangled dislocations without clear cell walls.

The caption states that the material is a Fee20Mne9Al-0.6C duplex phase steel and that the figure shows dislocation substructures in austenite (panels a–d) and ferrite (panels e, f) under different tensile strains.
The citing text states that for austenite unidirectional slips on the (111) plane were observed at 5 % tensile strain, with multidirectional slips appearing as strain increased.
The citing text states that after straining at 40 % unidirectional slip again determined the deformation mechanism in austenite, with a much smaller slip-line spacing than at low strain.
The citing text states that in ferrite dislocations dominated at 5 % strain and explosive dislocation multiplication developed into dislocation cells at 40 % strain.
The citing text concludes that austenite shows an obvious planar (plane) slip mechanism due to its high SFE, while ferrite shows wavy slip and forms dislocation cells.
